# runyard

> A lightweight, self-hosted tracker for ML training runs: one Go binary plus PostgreSQL. A Python library logs
> metrics, samples, logs and checkpoints; a web UI, an iOS app, a CLI and an MCP server read them; notifications go
> to ntfy, Slack, Discord, Telegram, a webhook or web push when a run finishes, fails or goes silent.

Key facts:

- Log from Python: `pip install runyard`, set `RUNYARD_SERVER` and `RUNYARD_API_KEY`, then
  `run = runyard.init(project=..., config=...)` and `run.log({...}, step=step)`. The library queues in a background
  thread and never stops training.
- No code change from tools that speak Weights & Biases (`RUNYARD_WANDB=1`), TensorBoard (`runyard watch ./logs`)
  or MLflow (`MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` pointed at the server).
- Agents read through the MCP server at `<server>/mcp` (streamable HTTP, `Authorization: Bearer <key>` when the
  server runs with `RUNYARD_AUTH`), or the `runyard` CLI with `--json`.
- A run is finished on a clean exit, failed on an exception and crashed after five minutes without a heartbeat.

## Docs

- [Run the server](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cobanov/runyard/main/docs/server.md): Docker Compose, storage, users and teams, API keys
- [Log runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cobanov/runyard/main/docs/logging.md): the Python library and every integration
- [Read runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cobanov/runyard/main/docs/reading.md): web UI, CLI, MCP tools and the REST API
- [Notifications and checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cobanov/runyard/main/docs/notifications.md): channels, rules and server-side checks
